tasks.short: Watch the student work, give encouraging feedback, note what went well, and message parents about the student's effort.

steps.what: Tutor watches the student work through problems
Tutor provides feedback using positive reinforcement techniques to build confidence
Tutor notes what went well and what to praise next time
Tutor reads the parent part of the note before sharing: it says what the student did and tried, in kind words, with nothing about other students
Tutor shares the parent part of the note with parents: by chat message today, by one release in the booking tool after the change

tasks.design: The session note in the booking tool ({OTHER}) has a field the tutor marks for parents; the tutor reads the marked part again and shares it with the parents in one release, so no separate chat message is written. Watching the student and giving encouraging feedback stay with the tutor.
tasks.previous_blocker: Tutors wrote notes for themselves and a separate chat message to parents.
tasks.enabler_now: Booking tools for tutors hold session notes and share chosen notes with parents.
tasks.still_hard: Praise that works for one student embarrasses another.
tasks.human_edge: Knowing when a quiet nod does more than a compliment.

reach.learn: Whether shared notes reduce parents' questions.

evidence.claim: Momoyoga offers class schedules, online booking and messaging with attendance reports.
Tutors hold minors' data, so parents must be informed and data kept to a minimum.

assumptions: Boundary: from the student's work to parents informed; lesson planning is outside.
Input contract: session notes by the tutor in the booking tool; parents' contact details from the intake; fallback is chat.
Watching and feedback do not change.
Parents read a shared note instead of a chat message; their time is about the same.
research_questions: Do parents ask fewer follow-up questions?

incremental.description: Tutor marks which note lines parents may see.

approvals.approved_version: The lines of the session note marked for parents, exactly as checked by the tutor in s3b, shared once with this student's parents in the booking tool; any later edit needs a new check.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: half of parents still want a chat message, so those are written as today (s4 55) (3.5); high: parents read the shared note (7.6).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Get the class material and worksheets, read and prepare, review the material with the student, make extra practice problems at the right level and share them.

steps.what: Student sends photos of the class material and worksheets
Tutor collects the class material and worksheets from chat and e-mail
Tutor reads the material and prepares the session
Tutor reviews class material with the student by discussing text and working solutions to problems
Tutor makes extra practice problems at the student's level

loop.input: The class worksheet, the topic and the student's level; no name or grades.
loop.output: Five practice problems with an answer key.
loop.check: Code checks each answer against a worked solution or key. The tutor reads every item: does it practise this week's class topic, is the level right, is the worked solution correct; items that do not fit are dropped or rewritten.
loop.stop: Approved by the tutor, or after two redrafts the tutor writes them.
loop.why_not_simpler: Problems must match this week's class material; a fixed bank does not.

steps.what: Tutor checks the final practice set before sharing: problems match this week's topic and level, answers are right, and it goes to this student's session
Tutor shares the practice problems with the student: by chat today, by one release in the booking tool after the change

tasks.design: Students upload photos of the week's class material to the session in the booking tool ({OTHER}) instead of sending them by chat, so the tutor finds them in one place. A bounded step drafts practice problems at the student's level with an answer key, and the tutor reads every item, checks the final set and shares it in one release. Reviewing the material with the student stays with the tutor.
tasks.previous_blocker: Material arrived in chat threads, and practice problems were written or searched for by hand.
tasks.enabler_now: Language models draft practice items at a set level; booking tools hold files per session.
tasks.still_hard: Drafted problems can be off-level or wrong, so every item needs reading.
tasks.human_edge: Seeing which step in a solution the student is guessing at.
tasks.altitude: The tutor checks drafted practice instead of writing it.

reach.learn: Whether tutor practice matches class work.

evidence.claim: LessonUp's lesson editor rewrites text at another difficulty and pulls word lists with definitions.
In a randomised trial with about 900 tutors, live AI suggestions raised topic mastery by 4 percentage points, and tutors flagged suggestions that were not grade-appropriate.

assumptions: Boundary: from the class material to shared practice; marking the practice is outside.
Input contract: class material from the student's school, uploaded by the student; fallback is chat.
Students upload photos instead of sending them by chat; their time is about the same and is shown as customer time.
Reviewing with the student does not change.
research_questions: How many drafted problems does the tutor drop?

already_counted.description: Tutor reads every drafted problem and its answer.

approvals.approved_version: The practice problems and answer key exactly as checked by the tutor in s5b, shared once to this student's session in the booking tool; any change needs a new check.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: in subjects like essay writing the tutor rewrites most drafted problems (s5 80) (12.7); high: maths and languages with clear keys (17.5).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Check understanding with questions during the session, give a short topic quiz, mark it, judge progress against the student's goals and record it.

steps.what: Tutor asks questions and watches the student solve problems to check understanding
Tutor writes a short quiz at the end of a topic
Student answers the quiz in the booking tool instead of on paper
Tutor marks the quiz by hand
Tutor judges progress against the student's goals throughout tutoring sessions
Tutor records progress in a document per student

tasks.design: Topic quizzes come from a question bank in the booking tool ({OTHER}) with closed items marked against a key, so marking by hand goes. Progress is recorded per goal in the student's record with the quiz scores next to it. Checking understanding and judging progress stay with the tutor; no AI evaluates the student.
tasks.previous_blocker: Quizzes were written and marked by hand and progress kept in loose documents.
tasks.enabler_now: Booking and learning tools hold question banks and mark closed items against a key.
tasks.still_hard: Open answers and reasoning still need the tutor's reading.
tasks.human_edge: Seeing that a right answer came from a lucky guess.

reach.learn: Whether recorded progress per goal helps parents.

evidence.claim: Learning tools mark closed quiz items against an answer key.
AI that evaluates learning outcomes in educational institutions is high-risk under Annex III point 3.

assumptions: Boundary: from the student's goals to the progress record; reports to parents are outside.
Input contract: goals agreed with student and parents at intake; question bank kept by the tutor; fallback is hand-written quizzes.
Checking and judging do not change.
Marking uses a fixed key, not a model.
s5 is the tutor's first record of each student's progress and keeps its full time.
research_questions: Does progress per goal show stalls sooner?

incremental.description: Tutor adds questions to the bank.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: subjects with mostly open answers, so the tutor still writes much of the quiz and marks by hand (s2 70, s3 100) (3.5); high: closed items marked against the key (18.1).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Find out how the student studies, teach study, note-taking and test-taking skills, prepare practice sheets on the student's own material, make a study plan and share them.

steps.what: Tutor finds out how the student studies and takes notes
Tutor teaches study skills, note-taking skills and test-taking strategies
Tutor prepares practice sheets on the student's own class texts

loop.input: A class text the student must learn and the strategy being taught (summary, key words, practice test).
loop.output: A practice sheet: a gap summary, a key-word list or a timed practice test with answers.
loop.check: Code checks every key word and answer appears in the class text. The tutor reads each sheet against the text: do the gap summaries say what the text says, do the questions test its main points; sheets that miss the point are rewritten or dropped.
loop.stop: Approved by the tutor, or after two redrafts the tutor makes it.
loop.why_not_simpler: Sheets must be built on this student's texts; templates cannot fill the content.

steps.what: Tutor makes a study plan for the next test with the student and checks the sheets that go with it
Tutor checks the final plan and sheets before sharing: dates count back from the right test, each sheet fits the plan, and it goes to this student
Tutor sends the study plan and sheets to the student: by chat today, by one release in the booking tool after the change

tasks.design: A bounded step drafts practice sheets on the student's own class texts (gap summaries, key-word lists, timed practice tests) and the tutor reads each one. A study planner template counts back from the test date in the booking tool ({OTHER}); the tutor fills it with the student, and the tutor checks plan and sheets together and shares them in one release. Teaching the skills stays with the tutor.
tasks.previous_blocker: Practice sheets were made by hand for each student and text.
tasks.enabler_now: Language models summarise texts and pull word lists for practice.
tasks.still_hard: A student who will not use the plan gains nothing from it.
tasks.human_edge: Finding the one habit that will change how this student revises.
tasks.altitude: The tutor checks drafted sheets instead of making them.

reach.learn: Whether students keep using the strategies alone.

evidence.claim: LessonUp's lesson editor summarises text and pulls word lists with definitions.
Tutors hold minors' grades and support needs, so the contract basis, informing parents and data minimisation apply.

assumptions: Boundary: from the student's goals to the shared plan; the test itself is outside.
Input contract: class texts uploaded by the student; test dates from the school's schedule; fallback is making sheets by hand.
Teaching the skills does not change.
No student name or grades go into the drafting step.
research_questions: Do students keep using the sheets between sessions?

incremental.description: Tutor reports drafts that miss the point of the text.

approvals.approved_version: The study plan and practice sheets exactly as checked by the tutor in s4b, shared once to this student's session in the booking tool; any change needs a new check.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: class texts are handwritten notes the step reads badly, so the tutor rewrites most sheets (s3 80) (11.6); high: students have digital class texts (17.6).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: The tutor keeps teaching, encouraging and judging progress; collecting material, writing practice and quizzes by hand, and separate parent messages shrink.
role.ambitious_version: A tutor who spends prep time on the students who are stuck.
